merge_ruling.for_merge: 'Niles' is an uncommon forename and it is identical on both, and the surnames differ in one letter that a worn impression confuses.
merge_ruling.against_merge: TWO ISSUES OF ONE PAPER, NEITHER SETTING BOTH, AND ROSE IS POPULATED HERE. 'Niles Rose' is the post-office return of 2 July 1834 (#c031); 'Niles Ross' the Democrat of 16 April 1834 (#c012) — two and a half months and two instruments apart, and no printing carries both spellings. The town holds rose_ruel beside rose_niles; the reading index holds seven Rose identities and five Ross, and the corpus sets Rose 151 times and Ross 50. Neither card is an anchor and T-0484 closed the letter-list side no_corroboration with 'no discriminator' written against it. D7.
